A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NSPO paper, with 32 pages and complete Appendices A–D. Extracted text and rendered page bodies match exactly after excluding the publication header and arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety-alignment and general-capability experiments in Tables 1–2, efficiency measurements in Table 3, and ablations, visualizations and case studies in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and Appendix C, including benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same NSPO procedure: constructing an SVD-based null-space projection, projecting safety gradients and removing the KL penalty. No method components change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PKU-SafeRLHF training data, general-domain data for projection construction, and seven safety plus seven general-capability benchmarks. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain DPO-H, DPO-S, DPO-Mix, SafeRLHF, PeCAN, MoCAN, W-DOOR and BFPO. The GRPO comparisons and appendix case-study comparators are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain identical model configurations, training budgets, sampling procedures, benchmark settings, evaluation metrics and judge prompts.

E4.justification: The projection-versus-KL ablations, projection-data and threshold sensitivity studies, training-data-size analysis, representation and gradient visualizations, and Appendix C case studies are identical.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 report the same standard deviations across three independent runs. Neither version adds or changes run information, uncertainty reporting or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All benchmark scores, efficiency measurements, plotted findings and qualitative outputs are unchanged, including Tables 1–3, Tables 5–6 and the case studies in Appendix C.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and their Appendix A proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about mitigating the alignment tax, preserving general capabilities, theoretical guarantees and safety-data efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of gradient projection, representation shifts, safety–utility trade-offs and data efficiency remain identical. No applicability qualifications or limitations are added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hardware and training-time information, Table 4 hyperparameters, evaluation prompts, and code/model/data access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, bibliography and positioning relative to previous alignment and constrained-RL methods are unchanged. The publication-status header does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint. Under review.' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'. The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 12 December 2025 to v2 dated 30 January 2026. Body language and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–6 retain identical content, captions, styling and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the header and arXiv stamp receive wording updates only.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication and version information while retaining identical scientific content and body presentation, including Appendices A–D. These metadata changes establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's evidence, reasoning, clarity or reproducibility.
